navigation.title: Navigation and Shell Chrome
navigation.purpose: Global chrome surrounding every NusaShell view: a top bar owns the drawer toggles, brand, room heading, context meter, and dock toggle; the left rail holds navigation and utilities.
navigation.howToOpen: Always visible when the NusaShell window is open.

sections.heading: Top bar
paragraphs: The top bar anchors the shell: hamburger and room-drawer toggles on the left, the NusaShell mark and room heading in the center, and the context meter plus conversation-dock toggle on the right. The context meter is visible only on Agent, where it opens the Context inspector; its ring fill tracks context usage while a data-connection state reflects WebSocket reachability. The room-drawer, context-meter, and dock toggles stay in the DOM on every route but are visible only while the Agent view is active (`.shell` carries `agent-active` only there); the narrow-width overlay backdrop is likewise scoped to the Agent surface so it can never cover a panel-less page. The room heading shows the active conversation title only while the Agent route owns the surface; every other route paints its own page label and asynchronous conversation updates cannot overwrite it.

Primary view titles are shown once in the global titlebar; duplicate in-page titles remain accessible to assistive technology without consuming visible space. Body-level toasts use the shell palette, a dismiss action, and a bounded mobile width.

sections.heading: Global navigation rail
paragraphs: The left rail orders Home, Agent, Skills, Learning, Automation, Plugins, Providers, Logs, Telemetry, and Settings as icon links. It can show icons with labels or icons only and remembers that choice locally. The install shortcut appears only while the browser offers installation; the desktop pet entry sits just above Settings (hidden at the <=720px overlay breakpoint): it surfaces install/launch status and opens the install dialog when the binary is missing.

Both Install and Pet drive hidden production-ID proxies (pwa-install-btn, pet-btn) so the shared pwa.js and pet-launcher.js modules work unchanged; the visible rail items are global-nav-install and global-nav-pet.

Below the nav breakpoints the rail becomes an off-canvas drawer: the top-bar nav toggle opens it and moves focus to the active rail item. It closes on backdrop click, Escape, selecting a nav item, or opening the room drawer/context dock — at the <=720px overlay breakpoint the rail and both conversation panels are mutually exclusive, so only one fixed overlay stays open at a time and no scrim can strand over a live panel — and focus returns to the toggle. Keyboard: Ctrl/Cmd+K or / focuses the search box on the current view, Escape dismisses dialogs, Ctrl/Cmd+N starts a new agent conversation when the Agent view is open.

Mobile Skills, Providers, Plugins, Logs, Learning, and Automation reopen at their index or primary tab when entered from navigation. In-page Back restores reading position; unsaved editor content is retained.

sections.heading: Offline screen
paragraphs: Full-window overlay shown whenever the backend is unreachable. It covers every view so no half-broken UI stays interactive: an explicit offline verdict shows it immediately, while closed/error/reconnecting states only cover after a short persistence window so quick reconnects never flicker. Recovery hides it instantly and Try again reloads the shell (service worker serves the cached shell while the server is down).

sections.heading: Device pairing gate
paragraphs: Full-window dialog shown when the backend requires device pairing (an unpaired non-loopback client). While the gate owns the screen, the offline overlay and view error toasts are suppressed so the pairing state is the single explanation. It renders pending/waiting, success, and terminal link states such as expired, rejected, already used, or invalid without offering a retry that cannot make the same link valid; transient backend/network failures can still be retried.

sections.heading: App loading layer
paragraphs: Full-window boot overlay shown while the shell loads its first data; it hides once the app is interactive.

home.title: Home
home.purpose: The launcher view: a grid of installed plugin apps. Each tile opens the plugin UI in a separate browser window. Searchable by name, id, or description and filterable by category.
home.howToOpen: Open NusaShell, or click the Home item in the left rail.

sections.heading: Filter row
paragraphs: A search input filters the app grid by name, id, or description. Category tabs narrow the grid to a single category (All plus every category present in the installed set, with an Uncategorized bucket when needed). Escape resets the search.

sections.heading: App grid
paragraphs: A responsive grid of plugin tiles. Each tile shows the plugin icon (including local manifest icons resolved for the browser), name, and a runtime status when active. Clicking a tile opens the plugin UI in a new browser window sized from the plugin manifest. While the backend requires pairing, the grid stays quiet so the pairing gate dominates; the Retry affordance reloads the list. At widths through 720px the same launcher opens a normal browser tab instead of a floating window.

agent.title: Agent
agent.purpose: The agent conversation view: a scrollable event stream of user and assistant rounds, thinking traces, tool calls, tasks, and artifacts; a composer with model, effort, route, workspace, and attachment controls; a left room drawer listing conversations; and a right context dock with Tasks, Subagents, and Context panels.
agent.howToOpen: Click the Agent item in the left rail, or open #agent.

sections.heading: Room drawer (conversations)
paragraphs: The left drawer lists every conversation room with search and a New chat action. On narrow widths it becomes an off-canvas panel toggled from the top bar; each row's action menu renames, compacts, or deletes the room. Deleted rooms disappear from the list and clear their per-room state.

sections.heading: Thread
paragraphs: The event stream renders the active conversation: user/assistant bubbles, Thinking disclosures, tool cards, task updates, and artifacts. Filter buttons narrow the stream to messages or activity; the Latest jump returns to the bottom. Long conversations are windowed: older rounds and archived pre-compaction chunks load on demand via the Load-older sentinel, keeping the scroll anchored. A running turn keeps every persisted round mounted on reload; Live Thinking deltas follow the thread only while the end marker is visible.

Compared to the old shell, the empty-state starter prompt chips are not rendered. ACP run details live inside the context dock Subagents panel (opened from the stream's subagent tool card), and the single-run transcript reader popup (acp-popup-overlay) is retained as a separate surface for delegation cards rendered inside transcripts — e.g. the Learning job transcript — where the dock is not the destination.

Thinking code blocks and tool Markdown details show language labels and code-editor controls. Relative file links in Thinking open the type-aware preview against the active workspace. Image, audio, and video tool previews are lazy; if loading fails, Retry remounts the preview and Preview file opens the shared file viewer. Text-file preview failures show a status-specific message with Retry and Close.

Question choices appear as full-width list rows with separators so long answer labels remain readable. File-preview failures are centered directly on the existing blue preview surface with Retry; the nested error card and its duplicate Close button are removed.

sections.heading: Tool runs strip
paragraphs: A collapsible strip above the composer lists in-flight tool runs with per-call elapsed time and a stop button on stoppable tools (exec). It hides once every job settles; orphaned running jobs are marked interrupted on turn done, error, or room switch.

sections.heading: Steer queue
paragraphs: A queued steering message waits for a safe boundary before joining the active turn. One compact row stacked inside the composer frame shows the pending text, promotes it into the transcript once applied, restores it to the composer when the backend rejects it, and cancels on demand.

sections.heading: Context dock
paragraphs: The right dock groups three panels behind tabs. Tasks shows the plan checklist with per-item delete; Subagents lists background ACP and delegate runs with an inline transcript; Context shows the live context-usage meter for the room and a Compact action that summarizes older messages while keeping the recent tail. The dock collapses into an overlay on narrow widths.

Parity note: the old acp-dock strip and acp-drawer live view are folded into this panel — subagent runs and their transcripts open inline here. The acp-popup peek overlay is not folded in: it survives as the single-run transcript reader (see 'Subagent transcript reader' below), opened by delegation cards rendered inside transcripts such as the Learning job view.

sections.heading: Subagent transcript reader
paragraphs: A modal dialog (role=dialog, aria-modal) that focuses a single subagent run: the header shows the agent name and the body renders that run's full transcript, hydrated on demand through acp.runs.get for historical runs the live cache no longer holds. It is the surviving single-run surface — the room-bound acp-drawer was retired when the dock panel took over.

Open: click a delegation/subagent card rendered inside a transcript (the Learning job transcript is the current surface; the same shared renderer drives any host that shows delegation cards). In the Agent view itself, prefer the dock Subagents panel — the stream's subagent tool card opens the dock, not this dialog.
Close: the × button, Escape, or clicking the dimmed overlay outside the dialog. Focus returns to the element that opened it.

sections.heading: Composer
paragraphs: The composer wraps the textarea with an attachment tray, the model/effort/route configuration popover, a workspace folder browser, and send/stop actions. The model popover groups model, effort, provider-route, and workspace selection; the route picker persists per room via agent.conversations.set-provider.

Model options show consistent Lucide SVG icons for Text plus Vision input, Audio input, and Video input only when the catalog advertises those capabilities. Searchable model labels and route values stay unchanged. With no selected workspace, the folder picker reads Home and Host home; a selected folder always shows its actual basename.
Model options show the display name above the muted original model ID. SVG modality icons remain vertically centered beside the two lines.

The model picker uses the enabled provider catalog. When no chat models are available it shows an empty disabled picker. File drops attach file content; in Electron, folder drops attach a folder path through the desktop bridge. In the browser, choose the workspace when a folder path is unavailable.
Returning to Agent reloads the enabled model catalog so newly imported models appear without reloading the window; valid model and effort selections are retained.

sections.heading: Mini window
paragraphs: The mini-window button beside the stream opens the conversation in a picture-in-picture window (document PiP when supported, else a ?mini=1 popup). Room diagnostics — ID, tool calls, message count — are owned by the Context dock tab. The button is desktop-only chrome: it hides at widths through 720px where there is no floating window surface. Electron hides this browser-only control.

skills.title: Skills
skills.purpose: The skills library: installable skill packages browsable, searched, inspected, edited, promoted, and rolled back from one workspace; learned and user-owned packages can also be deleted after confirmation.
skills.howToOpen: Click the Skills item in the left rail, or open #skills.

sections.heading: Header
paragraphs: Install button chooses a .skill or .zip package from disk.

sections.heading: Catalog
paragraphs: Searchable, owner/category-labelled list of installed skills with sync state and result counts; two persistent splitters divide the workspace index and the sheet file nav.
The mobile toolbar keeps its full content height; status and Install actions wrap as needed and stay above the library list.

sections.heading: Detail
paragraphs: Inspector shows owner, category, lifecycle state, usage stats, package files with a tree reader, and actions behind a menu. Delete is available for learned, user-owned, and built-in skills after confirmation; deleting a built-in records its removal so NusaShell does not automatically reinstall it. Plugin-owned skills point to uninstalling their owner, and Rollback remains available in the action menu. At widths through 720px, selecting a skill opens its detail page; Back preserves the selected package and search, while package files and their preview use separate steps.

plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.purpose: The plugins workspace: installed MCP servers and plugin apps in a searchable list with a detail inspector (state, tools, connection, preferences) and a three-source install dialog (catalog, GitHub, ZIP upload).
plugins.howToOpen: Click the Plugins item in the left rail, or open #plugins.

sections.heading: Header
paragraphs: Search, counts, sync state, update check, and actions to add a raw MCP server or open the install dialog.

sections.heading: Installed plugins
paragraphs: The list shows every installed plugin with runtime status; the inspector renders detail, state machine actions, tools, connection info, and autostart/autoupdate preferences. At widths through 720px the toolbar, filter row, and list hide while a plugin detail is open; the controller-mounted Back control returns to the filtered list and restores its scroll position.

sections.heading: Install dialog
paragraphs: A tabbed dialog installs plugins from the catalog, a GitHub repository (URL/owner-repo with optional subdirectory and ref), or a ZIP upload containing exactly one manifest.json. Errors surface in a banner inside the dialog.

providers.title: Providers
providers.purpose: Provider configuration: a two-tab workspace. The Providers tab lists configured LLM connections with a detail inspector (connection fields, models, Codex account, enable toggle, cache TTL and thinking-summary chips); the ACP tab manages spawn-only subagent workers (registry, probe, auth, modes, models).
providers.howToOpen: Click the Providers item in the left rail, or open #providers.

sections.heading: Tabs and toolbar
paragraphs: Two tabs switch between LLM providers and ACP subagents; each panel has its own search, counts, sync state, refresh, and add action. On mobile each tab starts with its own list and opens one selected detail at a time.

sections.heading: Configured providers
paragraphs: The list shows provider connections; the inspector renders connection fields, enable toggle, and the imported model list with filter. For Codex, the account and runtime card follows the connection/model grid in normal page flow. On mobile, Back returns to the same filtered provider list, and models and account details scroll with the page.

sections.heading: Codex accounts and runtime
paragraphs: The account card signs in with a device code: Sign in shows a code, Open sign-in page, Copy code, and Cancel sign in. The browser checks approval at the supplied interval until completion or the 15-minute expiry, then refreshes accounts. It never opens the backend machine browser. Import CLI reads local CLI credentials and Refresh reloads circuit state. A separate sibling runtime card reports version/path and downloads the runtime on demand.

Account quota shows both returned windows with used/available percentages and reset date/time. Optional limit_window_seconds labels actual 5-hour, Weekly, or Monthly periods; missing durations use neutral window labels and missing usage is unavailable.

sections.heading: ACP agents
paragraphs: The ACP panel registers spawn-only workers: search, add, edit, probe, refresh catalog, and delete, with detail cards for connection, auth methods, modes, and advertised models. On mobile, Back returns to the ACP list without clearing its search or selected worker.

The Models card includes Search ACP models. It filters the advertised catalog by model ID, name, description, or tier; no matching model is shown as an explicit empty result, and clearing the query restores the catalog without changing the preferred model.

learning.title: Learning
learning.purpose: The learning workbench: memory documents (About you / About agent), the searchable experience and record store, the knowledge graph atlas, and the learning activity log behind four tabs.
learning.howToOpen: Click the Learning item in the left rail, or open #learning.

sections.heading: Header stats
paragraphs: Live counters injected into the legend: memory items and graph edges (rendered vs total when the edge cap applies).

sections.heading: Tabs
paragraphs: Four tabs: Overview (stats, brief, recent learning, map), Memory (About you / About agent editors), Experiences (search + record lists), Activity (learning log). At widths through 720px the Overview tab collapses its document editors and knowledge map behind disclosure toggles, and the Memory atlas and Experiences tabs show either their list or one focused detail pane with a controller-mounted Back control.

Refresh spins during the full request and stops after completion or failure; sync status is announced nonvisually. On mobile, episode and Activity panels follow natural content height with page scrolling.

sections.heading: About You
paragraphs: The editable user memory document. Reload reads the persisted value again; Save changes replaces the complete user memory document through memory.user.update. The editor shows the 4000-character cap and allows an intentional empty document. The card expands across the available desktop canvas while keeping a compact inset and full-width editor on mobile. At widths through 720px the card collapses to a compact entry point behind an Edit disclosure toggle; status chips stay visible and an unsaved draft survives toggles.

sections.heading: About Agent
paragraphs: The editable agent-tier memory document. Reload reads the persisted value again; Save changes replaces the complete soul.md document through memory.agent.update. The editor shows the 4000-character cap and allows an intentional empty document. Changes remain separate from user.md and memory records. At widths through 720px the card collapses to a compact entry point behind an Edit disclosure toggle; status chips stay visible and an unsaved draft survives toggles.

sections.heading: Experience
paragraphs: Paginated list of recorded episodes from experience.list (newest first, 25 per page, Prev/Next controls). Each row shows the goal, outcome status, signals, and timestamp, with a per-row delete control that calls experience.delete after a styled confirm. Clicking a row loads experience.get and expands detail. Structured memory records from memory.list sit beside it; a selected record can be deleted with memory.delete after a styled confirm. The lists refresh on experience.recorded, experience.deleted, learning.job.started/done/error, and memory.updated. At widths through 720px an opened episode takes the focused detail pane; Back to episodes returns to the list, and re-opening the loaded episode or deleting it collapses back to the list.

sections.heading: Search bar
paragraphs: Hybrid search across memory and skills, with a kind filter (All, Skills, Memory) and a Search button. On phones the query and filter/action controls use separate full-width rows so none of the controls are clipped.

sections.heading: Results
paragraphs: Ranked search results with a count. With an empty query the pane lists all skills and records so content is visible immediately. Memory hits show a tier badge (user, agent, or record) next to the kind label. Records are retired from the Experience tab, not deleted here. Long content is collapsed to 3 lines; click to expand. Results refresh automatically when memory or skills change (via `memory.updated` / `skill.updated` events, debounced 300ms). At widths through 720px selecting a result opens it as a focused detail pane over the atlas; Back to atlas returns to the filtered result list and restores its scroll position.

sections.heading: Splitter
paragraphs: The atlas splitter divides the list column from the graph; it drags between 180px and viewport-200, steps 16px on arrow keys, and persists (clears below 860px).

sections.heading: Knowledge graph
paragraphs: Force-directed graph (vis-network) of skills, memory records, and their edges. Related edges are rebuilt from content similarity plus record metadata; stale edges to deleted nodes are removed. Used-with edges connect learning nodes observed together during one successful agent or learning-job turn. The backend coalesces unchanged graph rebuilds and emits a refresh event when newly derived edges are ready. Dense edge lines stay thin. Node size scales with the number of unique neighbouring nodes, making the most-connected hubs largest; hover text includes the relation count. Zooming out preserves most of that size contrast so nearby relation counts remain visually distinct instead of collapsing to the same rasterized radius. After its bounded physics pass, a full layout keeps the force-directed angular grouping but places highly connected hubs toward the center and low-degree or isolated nodes toward a compact perimeter ring without detaching them from the main cluster, then resolves residual collisions before freezing. The restrained archipelago palette maps skills to ocean blue, records to earth brown, user memory to leaf green, and edges to deeper ocean, mangrove, or sand tones. Reload fetches the graph and performs this full relayout; Fit fits it to view. When the backend has more than 2,000 edges, the browser renders the strongest 2,000 and shows the rendered/total count; the complete edge set remains available to the backend. Legend distinguishes Skill, Record, Related, and Used-with edges. The graph refreshes automatically when memory or skills change, a learning job finishes, or the background graph build completes (via `memory.updated` / `skill.updated` / `learning.job.done` / `learning.graph.updated` events, coalesced with a 300ms debounce); automatic refreshes keep existing node positions and the current zoom/pan, laying out only additions, so the graph and the user's viewport stay still while idle. On narrow screens results and graph stack into separate bounded panes with their own scrollable result list. On the Overview tab at widths through 720px the map card collapses behind a Show map disclosure that redraws and refits the graph when revealed.
The Overview map and Activity feed share the global Learning Refresh; they do not render duplicate refresh buttons. Global refresh retains the current graph viewport and Activity page.

sections.heading: Learning log
paragraphs: Learning-job activity feed from the trajectory log (experience extraction, consolidation, skill jobs, edge building, decay, prune), newest first. The feed reads one bounded 50-event page at a time instead of loading the full history; Previous and Next use stable cursors; the single Learning Refresh reloads the current page alongside the other Learning data. Job entries show a status badge (done or error); failures use a concise automatic-processing message rather than exposing a verbose provider body. Each entry has a compact Source <title> line, saved outcomes (kind + snippet) or an explicit Nothing to save. line, and per-type extras. A running indicator appears at the top while a learning job is in-flight. Inert recent-job status chips are not displayed. At widths through 720px the feed flows in the single page scroll instead of a nested scroll cage.

automation.title: Automation
automation.purpose: The automation control room: workflows, runs, schedules, and event records in one browse column with stat cards, a mode switch, search, and an inspector with detail, steer/delete actions, and the YAML workflow editor.
automation.howToOpen: Click the Automation item in the left rail, or open #automation.

sections.heading: Header
paragraphs: Refresh, sync state, and the New workflow action; errors collapse into a retry banner.

sections.heading: Stats
paragraphs: Counts of runnable, needs-attention, in-progress, and waiting items across workflows and runs.

sections.heading: Browse
paragraphs: The mode switch filters workflows, runs, and event records; search narrows the list by name or state; the schedule rail lists upcoming runs. Blocked workflows show a callout with the reason and an enable-provider action when a capability is disabled.

On mobile through 720px, Runs and Events use a full-width feed with sticky tabs and search. Opening a record shows its detail separately; Back returns to the same filter, selection and reading position. Workflow overview and desktop split panes remain available.

sections.heading: Inspector and editor
paragraphs: The inspector renders the selected workflow (capabilities, enable/run/delete/steer actions), run (per-step progress and output, cancel/steer), or the YAML editor with validation.

logs.title: Logs
logs.purpose: The runtime log tail: a filterable, searchable, followable entry list with a detail reader, bounded to a 2,000-entry ring buffer.
logs.howToOpen: Click the Logs item in the left rail, or open #logs.

sections.heading: Filters
paragraphs: Search by source or message, filter by level, and follow the live tail; Refresh reloads and Clear wipes the buffer after confirmation.

sections.heading: List and detail
paragraphs: The list renders entries newest-last with a Latest jump when scrolled up; the detail pane shows source, level, time, id, and the full message. At widths through 720px the page stays viewport-bound and the entry list scrolls inside the bounded workspace card — Follow and Latest target that inner list — while selecting an entry opens one detail page; Back restores the filtered list and preserves follow-tail behavior.

settings.title: Settings
settings.purpose: Instance settings grouped behind an eight-item rail (Overview, Models, Agent, Context & memory, Media, Web, Interface, Remote access). Fields render into the panels with ids of the form settings-field-<key>; a dirty state opens a review bar with per-change revert before saving.
settings.howToOpen: Click the Settings item in the left rail, or open #settings.

sections.heading: Header and save bar
paragraphs: Refresh and sync state sit in the header; edits mark fields dirty and open the save bar with a change count, a review dialog with per-change revert, discard, and save. The Fix action jumps to the first invalid field.

sections.heading: Section rail
paragraphs: The rail jumps to a settings section; search filters fields across all sections and shows an empty state when nothing matches. The disk banner warns about low space when reported.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: The overview panel summarizes the instance with a tile per capability (state on/install/off), delegate/tool-round/compaction defaults, and a responsive status panel for version, data directory with Copy, and remote-access state. Clicking a tile scrolls to its card.

sections.heading: Settings fields
paragraphs: Every settings field renders with id settings-field-<key> inside its section panel; these ids are generated per field at render time. Model fields use styled selects; secrets never echo stored values.

sections.heading: Special cards
paragraphs: The media section adds install/status cards for offline STT and TTS (model/voice pickers, install + stop actions, progress, per-OS install guides) and the desktop pet card; Interface adds the font segment picker with a live specimen and the compact-sidebar toggle; Models adds the preferred model select.

sections.heading: Remote access
paragraphs: The remote panel toggles remote access and drives device pairing: generate a link, show the QR, list paired sessions, revoke all, and approve or reject pending devices through the approval overlay.

telemetry.title: Telemetry
telemetry.purpose: Usage and cost telemetry: period presets plus provider/model filters drive four stat cards (spend, requests, tokens, cache hit, blended $/1M), a spend-trend chart, a token-mix stack, and model/provider breakdowns.
telemetry.howToOpen: Click the Telemetry item in the left rail, or open #telemetry.

sections.heading: Header
paragraphs: Period presets (1h to All), provider and model filter menus, refresh, and an error banner with retry; the period copy summarizes the loaded report.

sections.heading: Summary metrics
paragraphs: Headline cards for the selected period.

sections.heading: Spend trend
paragraphs: Estimated spend over time in the selected period.

sections.heading: Token mix
paragraphs: Input, output, cache-read, and cache-write token mix with a legend and total.

sections.heading: By model
paragraphs: Usage concentration by model.

sections.heading: By provider
paragraphs: Usage routing by provider.

global-nav-toggle.label: Navigation toggle
global-nav-toggle.action: Toggles the global navigation rail open or closed.

room-drawer-toggle.label: Conversations drawer toggle
room-drawer-toggle.action: Toggles the room drawer (conversation list) open or closed.
room-drawer-toggle.notes: Agent-only control: always present in the top-bar DOM but hidden on every non-Agent route (`.shell:not(.agent-active)` display:nones it); leaving Agent also closes any open overlay panel so the shared backdrop cannot strand over a panel-less page.

context-meter.label: Context meter
context-meter.action: Opens the context dock Context panel; ring fill tracks the active room context usage.
context-meter.notes: Agent-only control: it is hidden on non-Agent routes because only Agent owns the Context inspector. Doubles as the backend connection indicator: data-connection mirrors WebSocket reachability and its title reads Backend connected / Backend <state>. Context thresholds: data-context=high at >=80%, critical at >=95% of the active model context window.

context-dock-toggle.label: Dock toggle
context-dock-toggle.action: Toggles the conversation context dock open or closed.
context-dock-toggle.notes: Agent-only control: always present in the top-bar DOM but hidden on every non-Agent route (`.shell:not(.agent-active)` display:nones it); leaving Agent also closes any open overlay panel so the shared backdrop cannot strand over a panel-less page.

global-nav.label: Global navigation rail
global-nav.notes: Left icon rail holding the 11 route items plus Install, Pet, Settings, and the compact-mode toggle.

global-nav-item.label: Navigation items
global-nav-item.action: Each item routes the shell to its view via hash links (#home, #agent, #skills, #learning, #automation, #plugins, #providers, #logs, #telemetry, #settings).
global-nav-item.notes: Anchors with data-global-route carrying the hash route; the active one carries is-active and aria-current=page.

global-nav-expand.label: Expand sidebar
global-nav-expand.action: Toggles the rail between icon-only and icon+label modes; the choice persists in localStorage (nusashell.sidebarMode).
global-nav-expand.notes: At <=720px the rail is an always-labelled overlay drawer, so the same footer slot becomes a Close sidebar action that dismisses the drawer instead of toggling a mode it cannot show.

global-nav-install.label: Install app
global-nav-install.action: Shows only while the browser offers PWA installation; installs NusaShell as an app.
global-nav-install.notes: Drives the hidden pwa-install-btn proxy so js/pwa.js keeps working.

global-nav-pet.label: Desktop pet
global-nav-pet.action: Opens the desktop pet launcher: routes to Settings pet card and dispatches the pet launcher event.
global-nav-pet.notes: Drives the hidden pet-btn proxy via nusashell:open-pet-launcher so js/pet-launcher.js keeps working; a status dot on the icon reflects install state. Hidden at widths through 720px — the pet launcher is a desktop-only affordance.

pwa-install-btn.label: Install app proxy
pwa-install-btn.action: Hidden production-ID proxy bound by js/pwa.js initInstallButton; global-nav-install is the visible affordance.
pwa-install-btn.notes: Kept inside a hidden wrapper so module state flips never render a duplicate control.

pet-btn.label: Desktop pet proxy
pet-btn.action: Hidden production-ID proxy bound by js/pet-launcher.js (install dialog, launch toggle).
pet-btn.notes: Kept inside a hidden wrapper; global-nav-pet is the visible affordance.

mobile-nav-backdrop.label: Navigation backdrop
mobile-nav-backdrop.action: Click to close the open navigation drawer on small screens.

offline-screen.label: Offline screen
offline-screen.notes: Full-window overlay covering every view while the backend is unreachable; hidden again the moment the connection reopens.

offline-retry-btn.label: Try again
offline-retry-btn.notes: Reloads the shell; the service worker serves the cached app while the server is down.

pairing-gate.label: Device pairing gate
pairing-gate.notes: Full-window dialog shown when the backend requires device pairing; owns the screen while PAIRING_REQUIRED or PAIRING_SESSION_EXPIRED (the latter shows re-pair copy for a previously paired device).

pairing-gate-title.label: Pairing gate title
pairing-gate-title.notes: Receives focus when the gate opens.

pairing-gate-intro.label: Pairing gate explanation
pairing-gate-intro.notes: Explains either the pairing requirement or that remote access is disabled on the host.

pairing-help.label: Pairing help
pairing-help.notes: Explains how to open the host QR and pair.

pairing-help-btn.label: Pairing help toggle
pairing-help-btn.action: Shows or hides the pairing help panel.

page-loading.label: Loading layer
page-loading.notes: Full-window boot overlay removed once the shell is interactive.

home-search.label: App search
home-search.action: Filters installed apps by name, id, or description. Escape clears the query.

home-category-tabs.label: App categories
home-category-tabs.action: Filters the app grid to a single category; All resets. Hidden until categories load.

home-app-grid.label: App grid
home-app-grid.action: Click an app tile to open its plugin UI through the shared launcher: a separate floating window on desktop, a normal browser tab at widths through 720px.

home-app-count.label: App count
home-app-count.notes: Visible vs installed count while a filter is active.

home-app-message.label: Launcher status
home-app-message.notes: Loading, empty, error, and pairing-quiet states for the launcher.

home-app-retry.label: Retry loading apps
home-app-retry.action: Reloads the app grid after a failed fetch.

room-drawer.label: Room drawer
room-drawer.notes: Left drawer listing conversation rooms; slides in as an overlay on narrow widths.

room-search-input.label: Conversation search
room-search-input.notes: Filters room titles in real time.

room-list.label: Conversation list
room-list.notes: Interactive Agent rooms only; each row's action menu renames, compacts, or deletes the room.

new-chat.label: New chat
new-chat.action: Starts a temporary local draft and focuses the composer; the durable conversation is created when the first user message is sent.

conversation-surface.label: Agent view surface
conversation-surface.notes: Routed section carrying data-view="agent"; replaces the old agent-shell/agent-conversation containers.

event-stream.label: Event stream
event-stream.notes: Scrollable conversation log (aria-busy while a turn runs); windowed history plus archived chunks behind the load-older sentinel.

agent-thread.label: Thread log
agent-thread.notes: Runtime wrapper around event-stream created for the mini-window (document PiP) path; display:contents so layout is unchanged. The stream renders user/assistant bubbles, Thinking disclosures, tool cards, tasks, and artifacts with preserved disclosure state across refreshes.

stream-activity.label: Stream activity
stream-activity.notes: Animated status line under the stream (working, auto-continue, compaction) with aria-live announcements.

jump-latest.label: Jump to latest
jump-latest.action: Scrolls the stream to the newest events.

event-filters.label: Stream filters
event-filters.action: Narrows the stream to all events, messages only, or activity only.

load-older-events.label: Load older messages
load-older-events.action: Reveals older in-memory events first, then archived pre-compaction chunks (agent.conversations.chunk), keeping the scroll position anchored.

tool-job-strip.label: Tool calls strip
tool-job-strip.notes: In-flight tool calls for the current turn.

tool-job-list.label: Tool job list
tool-job-list.notes: Rows of in-flight tool calls with elapsed time.

tool-job-stop.label: Stop tool run
tool-job-stop.action: Stops a stoppable tool call (exec) via agent.tools.stop.

agent-steer-queue.label: Steer queue
agent-steer-queue.notes: One compact queued-steer row stacked inside the composer frame (icon, queued text, cancel), waiting for a safe boundary; hidden while the queue is empty.

context-dock.label: Context dock
context-dock.notes: Right dock grouping Tasks, Subagents, and Context panels behind tabs; overlay panel on narrow widths.

tab-tasks.label: Tasks tab
tab-tasks.action: Opens the task plan checklist panel.

panel-tasks.label: Tasks panel
panel-tasks.notes: Task plan checklist for the active conversation.

dock-task-delete.label: Delete task
dock-task-delete.action: Deletes a todo item via agent.todos.delete.

tab-subagents.label: Subagents tab
tab-subagents.action: Opens the background subagent runs panel.

panel-subagents.label: Subagents panel
panel-subagents.notes: Background ACP and delegate runs for the room; hidden until a run exists. Replaces the old acp-dock strip.

subagent-trigger.label: Subagent picker
subagent-trigger.action: Opens the subagent run list inside the dock panel.

subagent-options.label: Subagent run list
subagent-options.action: Lists parallel subagent runs with status dots.

subagent-detail.label: Subagent detail
subagent-detail.notes: Inline detail for the selected run: status, agent, elapsed time, objective, and transcript. Replaces the old acp-drawer live view; the single-run acp-popup reader remains a separate surface opened from delegation cards.

acp-popup-overlay.label: Subagent reader overlay
acp-popup-overlay.action: Click outside the dialog to close the transcript reader.

acp-popup.label: Subagent transcript reader
acp-popup.notes: Modal single-run reader (role=dialog, aria-modal). Opened by delegation cards rendered inside transcripts (e.g. the Learning job transcript); Escape, the close button, or an overlay click dismisses it.

acp-popup-close.label: Close subagent reader
acp-popup-close.action: Closes the transcript reader and returns focus to the opener.

acp-popup-title.label: Subagent reader title
acp-popup-title.notes: Shows the selected run's agent name.

acp-popup-body.label: Subagent reader body
acp-popup-body.notes: Hosts the single run transcript; historical runs are hydrated on demand through acp.runs.get.

panel-context.label: Context panel
panel-context.notes: Context-usage detail for the active room, synced with the top-bar context meter.

context-compact.label: Compact context
context-compact.action: Starts manual compaction for the active conversation via agent.conversations.compact.
context-compact.notes: Disabled while the room has no conversation, a turn is running, or compaction is already in progress. The same action is in each room's action menu. A room with nothing older to summarize, or a model that compacts on the provider, finishes with a status message instead of a summary pass.

message-input.label: Message input
message-input.shortcut: Ctrl+Enter / ⌘↩ to send; Escape closes dialogs

attachment-input.label: File input
attachment-input.notes: Hidden file picker for images, PDFs, and text files.

model-config-trigger.label: Model configuration
model-config-trigger.action: Opens the composer configuration popover (model, effort, route, workspace).

model-config-summary.label: Model summary
model-config-summary.notes: Current model label inside the config trigger.

effort-config-summary.label: Effort summary
effort-config-summary.notes: Current effort label inside the config trigger.

model-config-popover.label: Model configuration popover
model-config-popover.notes: Groups model, effort, provider-route, and workspace selection.

model-select.label: Model picker
model-select.action: Chooses the active model for the next turn.
model-select.notes: Slim Select instance populated from the provider catalog.

effort-select.label: Effort picker
effort-select.action: Chooses the reasoning effort for the next turn.

route-select.label: Provider route picker
route-select.action: Selects the per-conversation provider route (Auto, upstream provider, or Codex account); persisted via agent.conversations.set-provider.

workspace-browser-trigger.label: Workspace selector
workspace-browser-trigger.action: Opens the in-app workspace folder browser (server-side directories via agent.workspace.list-dirs).

workspace-browser-view.label: Workspace browser
workspace-browser-view.notes: In-app folder browser listing server-side directories via agent.workspace.list-dirs.

workspace-browser-back.label: Back to model config
workspace-browser-back.action: Returns from the workspace browser to the model configuration view.

workspace-up.label: Parent folder
workspace-up.action: Navigates the workspace browser to the parent directory.

workspace-breadcrumbs.label: Workspace breadcrumbs
workspace-breadcrumbs.notes: Clickable path segments for the browsed folder.

workspace-search.label: Workspace search
workspace-search.action: Filters folders in the current directory.

workspace-use-folder.label: Use this folder
workspace-use-folder.action: Confirms the browsed folder as the conversation workspace.

ask-popover.label: Ask popover
ask-popover.notes: Inline confirmation popover for agent ask-style tool requests (aria-live=assertive).

stop-turn-button.label: Stop turn
stop-turn-button.action: Cancels the running turn; partial output is kept and marked interrupted.

mini-window-btn.label: Mini window
mini-window-btn.notes: Opens the picture-in-picture mini window (Document PiP on Chromium, popup fallback elsewhere) showing the live agent thread. Appears in the stream toolbar for an active browser conversation; hidden in Electron until its mini-window flow is supported. Hidden at widths through 720px — there is no floating picture-in-picture surface on the phone layout.

skills-install.label: Install skill
skills-install.notes: Opens file picker to install a .skill or .zip archive.

skill-file-input.label: Skill package input
skill-file-input.notes: Hidden file picker accepting .skill and .zip packages.

skills-splitter-1.label: Workspace index splitter
skills-splitter-1.action: Drags the index column between 150-450px; keyboard arrows step 16px; persists per session.

skills-splitter-2.label: Sheet nav splitter
skills-splitter-2.action: Drags the sheet file-nav column between 150-500px; drops out below 720px.

skill-editor-title.label: Editor title
skill-editor-title.notes: Shows the selected skill name or 'No file selected'.

skill-detail-owner.label: Skill owner
skill-detail-owner.notes: Owner label in the detail eyebrow.

skill-detail-category.label: Skill category
skill-detail-category.notes: Category label in the detail eyebrow.

skill-editor-empty.label: Editor empty state
skill-editor-empty.notes: Empty state shown when no file is selected. Prompts user to pick a file from the skill tree.

skill-status-badge.label: Skill status
skill-status-badge.notes: Promotion status: candidate, experimental, validated, trusted, deprecated, or retired.

skill-version-meta.label: Skill version
skill-version-meta.notes: Shows Version and ActiveVersion for the selected skill.

skills-promote.label: Promote skill
skills-promote.action: Promotes an experimental or validated skill via skills.promote.

skills-rollback-version.label: Rollback version
skills-rollback-version.notes: Custom select of skill versions used by Rollback.

skills-rollback.label: Rollback skill
skills-rollback.action: Rolls the selected skill back to the chosen version via skills.rollback.

skills-delete.label: Delete skill
skills-delete.action: Deletes a learned or user-owned skill after confirmation via skills.delete. Hidden for builtin and plugin-owned skills.

skills-mobile-back.label: Back to skills
skills-mobile-back.action: Returns to the filtered skill list while keeping the selected package open.

skill-file-back.label: Back to package files
skill-file-back.action: Returns from the file preview to the selected package tree without closing the package.

skill-file-viewer.label: Skill file viewer
skill-file-viewer.notes: Shows file content when a file is clicked in the skill tree.

skill-files-tree.label: Package file tree
skill-files-tree.notes: Files inside the selected skill package; each row opens the reader.

skill-file-content.label: Skill file content
skill-file-content.notes: Pre-formatted text content of the opened skill file.

skill-actions-guidance.label: Skill ownership guidance
skill-actions-guidance.notes: Explains when deletion is unavailable for built-in or plugin-owned skills.

plugins-add-mcp.label: Add MCP
plugins-add-mcp.action: Opens the native MCP server editor.

plugins-filter.label: Connection filter
plugins-filter.action: Filters the plugin list by connection state (all, connected, disconnected).

plugins-detail-open-ui.label: Open UI
plugins-detail-open-ui.action: Opens the selected MCP + UI plugin through the shared plugin launcher (served at /plugins/<id>/): a separate floating window on desktop, a normal browser tab at widths through 720px. Hidden for MCP-only entries.

plugins-detail-start.label: Start
plugins-detail-start.action: Connects the selected MCP server or plugin and lists its tools.

plugins-detail-restart.label: Restart
plugins-detail-restart.action: Stops then starts the selected MCP server or plugin.

plugins-detail-update.label: Update
plugins-detail-update.action: Updates a catalog plugin in place to its latest release (plugin.update). Appears only when a newer catalog version is available; the label shows the target version.

plugins-detail-edit.label: Edit
plugins-detail-edit.action: Opens the MCP server editor for the selected native MCP entry. Hidden for plugins.

plugins-tools-list.label: Tools list
plugins-tools-list.notes: Lists the tools exposed by the connected MCP server or plugin with name and description.

plugins-connection-list.label: Connection info
plugins-connection-list.notes: Manifest and connection fields for the selected plugin.

plugins-detail-autostart.label: Start automatically
plugins-detail-autostart.action: Launches this MCP server or plugin automatically when NusaShell starts (plugin.set_autostart).

plugins-autoupdate-row.label: Auto update row
plugins-autoupdate-row.notes: Preference row shown only for catalog-managed plugins; contains the auto-update switch.

plugins-detail-autoupdate.label: Auto update
plugins-detail-autoupdate.action: Updates this catalog plugin automatically when a new version is released (plugin.set_autoupdate). Shown only for catalog-managed plugins.

plugins-install-error.label: Install error banner
plugins-install-error.notes: Inline error shown inside the installer when an install attempt fails; cleared on tab switch or dialog close.

plugins-catalog-search.label: Plugin catalog search
plugins-catalog-search.action: Filters the plugin catalog by name, id, or description.

plugins-install-confirm.label: Confirm install
plugins-install-confirm.action: Confirms the current install source (GitHub or ZIP).

providers-mobile-back.label: Back to connections
providers-mobile-back.action: Returns to the filtered provider list while keeping the selected connection.

provider-cache-ttl.label: Prompt cache TTL
provider-cache-ttl.action: Selects the prompt-cache duration sent to this provider when Settings prompt caching is on, or off to skip caching for this provider. Messages and OpenRouter chat offer 5m/1h/off; Responses and other Chat hosts offer 30m/off.
provider-cache-ttl.notes: Buttons inside the provider detail pane (class provider-cache-ttl-chip). The last chip is off. Empty stored TTL still defaults to the first duration. The registry card shows the selected value only.

provider-reasoning-summary.label: Thinking summary
provider-reasoning-summary.action: Selects how verbose the visible Codex thinking summary should be: auto, concise, detailed, or none.
provider-reasoning-summary.notes: Available only for Codex-kind providers. The selected value is stored per provider and applies on the next turn; none suppresses the visible summary without disabling model reasoning.

providers-codex-login.label: Sign in with ChatGPT
providers-codex-login.action: Starts Codex OAuth PKCE login via ai.codex.login.

providers-codex-import.label: Import from Codex CLI
providers-codex-import.action: Imports ChatGPT auth from the local Codex CLI auth.json via ai.codex.import.

providers-codex-refresh.label: Refresh Codex circuits
providers-codex-refresh.action: Polls account usage circuits via ai.codex.refresh-circuits then reloads the accounts list.

codex-runtime-card.label: Codex runtime card
codex-runtime-card.notes: Injected inside the Codex card for codex providers: reports the embedded Codex runtime state.

codex-runtime-status.label: Codex runtime status
codex-runtime-status.notes: Shows installed version/path, downloading, or not-installed from ai.codex.runtime.status.

codex-runtime-download-btn.label: Download Codex runtime
codex-runtime-download-btn.action: Downloads the managed Codex CLI binary via ai.codex.runtime.download.

acp-mobile-back.label: Back to connections
acp-mobile-back.action: Returns to the ACP list while keeping its search and selected worker.

learning-tab-overview.label: Overview tab
learning-tab-overview.action: Shows stats, the carried brief, recent learning, and the knowledge map.

learning-tab-memory.label: Memory tab
learning-tab-memory.notes: Shows the editable always-injected user memory document.
learning-tab-memory.action: Opens the About you / About agent editors.

learning-tab-experiences.label: Experiences tab
learning-tab-experiences.notes: Shows recorded episodes and structured memory records.
learning-tab-experiences.action: Opens experience and memory record search.

learning-user-status.label: User memory status
learning-user-status.notes: Reports whether user memory is loaded, empty, saved, or unavailable.

learning-user-memory.label: User memory editor
learning-user-memory.action: Edits the complete user memory document.

learning-user-reload.label: Reload user memory
learning-user-reload.action: Discards the current draft and reloads the persisted user memory document.

learning-user-save.label: Save user memory
learning-user-save.action: Replaces the persisted user memory document.

learning-agent-status.label: Soul memory status
learning-agent-status.notes: Reports whether soul.md is loaded, empty, saved, or unavailable.

learning-agent-reload.label: Reload soul memory
learning-agent-reload.action: Discards the current draft and reloads the persisted soul.md document.

learning-experience-list.label: Experience list
learning-experience-list.notes: Read-only episodes from experience.list, newest first. Click a row to load experience.get.

learning-records-list.label: Memory records list
learning-records-list.notes: Structured MemoryRecord rows from memory.list (tier record). Select a row, then delete.

learning-record-delete.label: Delete memory record
learning-record-delete.action: Calls memory.delete after a styled confirm. Removes the record, its graph edges, and its retrieval presence permanently. Disabled until a record is selected.

learning-graph-fit.label: Fit to view
learning-graph-fit.action: Fits the graph to the viewport.

learning-log.label: Learning log
learning-log.notes: Bounded 50-event trajectory page; job entries may have done/error/skipped status badges. Failed entries show a concise automatic-processing message; raw provider diagnostics stay server-side.

learning-log-prev.label: Previous learning log page
learning-log-prev.action: Returns to the preceding newer 50-event page.

learning-log-next.label: Next learning log page
learning-log-next.action: Loads the next older 50-event page with the trajectory cursor.

automation-mode-switch.label: Mode switch
automation-mode-switch.action: Filters the browse list between workflows, runs, and events.

logs-search.label: Log search
logs-search.action: Filters entries by source or message.

logs-latest.label: Jump to latest
logs-latest.action: Scrolls to the newest entries and resumes follow.

logs-pending-count.label: Pending entries
logs-pending-count.action: New entries arrived while scrolled up.

logs-workspace.label: Log list and detail workspace
logs-workspace.notes: Shows the list and entry detail side by side on desktop, and one pane at a time on mobile.

logs-mobile-back.label: Back to logs
logs-mobile-back.action: Returns to the filtered log list and preserves follow-tail state.

settings-jump-overview.label: Overview section
settings-jump-overview.action: Scrolls to the overview settings panel.

settings-jump-models.label: Models section
settings-jump-models.action: Scrolls to the models settings panel.

settings-jump-agent.label: Agent section
settings-jump-agent.action: Scrolls to the agent settings panel.

settings-jump-context.label: Context section
settings-jump-context.action: Scrolls to the context settings panel.

settings-jump-media.label: Media section
settings-jump-media.action: Scrolls to the media settings panel.

settings-jump-web.label: Web section
settings-jump-web.action: Scrolls to the web settings panel.

settings-jump-interface.label: Interface section
settings-jump-interface.action: Scrolls to the interface settings panel.

settings-jump-remote.label: Remote section
settings-jump-remote.action: Scrolls to the remote settings panel.

settings-overview-summary.label: Overview summary
settings-overview-summary.notes: Shows delegate/tool-round/compaction defaults and a responsive version, data-directory copy, and remote-access status panel.

settings-field-delegate_model.label: Delegate model
settings-field-delegate_model.notes: Model used for delegated subagent turns. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-review_model.label: Review model
settings-field-review_model.notes: Model used by the review/learning passes. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-compaction_model.label: Compaction model
settings-field-compaction_model.notes: Model used for context compaction summaries. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-embedding_model.label: Embedding model
settings-field-embedding_model.notes: Model used for memory embeddings. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-user_prompt.label: User instructions
settings-field-user_prompt.notes: Custom instructions appended to the system prompt. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-max_tool_rounds.label: Max tool rounds
settings-field-max_tool_rounds.notes: Tool-call rounds allowed per turn. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-repeated_tool_limit.label: Repeated tool limit
settings-field-repeated_tool_limit.notes: Identical tool calls allowed before the turn stops. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-max_parallel_tools.label: Max parallel tools
settings-field-max_parallel_tools.notes: Tool calls allowed to run concurrently. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-max_auto_continues.label: Auto continues
settings-field-max_auto_continues.notes: Automatic continuations allowed per turn. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-slow_down.label: Slow down
settings-field-slow_down.notes: Seconds to wait before every round of every conversation; 0 disables. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-max_output_tokens.label: Max output tokens
settings-field-max_output_tokens.notes: Default completion token limit when the model does not advertise one. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-temperature.label: Temperature
settings-field-temperature.notes: Sampling temperature sent to the provider. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-top_p.label: Top P
settings-field-top_p.notes: Nucleus sampling cutoff sent to the provider. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-top_k.label: Top K
settings-field-top_k.notes: Highest-probability token cutoff for Anthropic models. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-frequency_penalty.label: Frequency penalty
settings-field-frequency_penalty.notes: Penalty for tokens the model has already used. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-presence_penalty.label: Presence penalty
settings-field-presence_penalty.notes: Penalty for tokens that have appeared at least once. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-plugin_contract_mode.label: Plugin contract mode
settings-field-plugin_contract_mode.notes: How strictly plugin tool contracts are enforced. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-compaction_workflow.label: Compaction workflow
settings-field-compaction_workflow.notes: Which compaction pipeline summarizes context. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-max_input_tokens.label: Max input tokens
settings-field-max_input_tokens.notes: Context budget that triggers compaction. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-compaction_threshold.label: Compaction threshold
settings-field-compaction_threshold.notes: Fraction of the context window that triggers compaction. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-compaction_summary_max_to.label: Summary max tokens
settings-field-compaction_summary_max_to.notes: Cap on compaction summary output length. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-compaction_summary_min_ch.label: Summary min chars
settings-field-compaction_summary_min_ch.notes: Minimum summary length accepted before retry. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-prompt_caching.label: Prompt caching
settings-field-prompt_caching.notes: Enables provider prompt caching where supported. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-learner_nudge_interval.label: Learner nudge interval
settings-field-learner_nudge_interval.notes: Rounds between learning nudges. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-project_memory_base.label: Project memory base
settings-field-project_memory_base.notes: How much project memory seeds new rooms. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-vision_model.label: Vision fallback model
settings-field-vision_model.notes: Model used when the active model lacks vision. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-audio_model.label: Audio fallback model
settings-field-audio_model.notes: Model used for audio inputs. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-video_model.label: Video fallback model
settings-field-video_model.notes: Model used for video inputs. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-stt_offline_model.label: Offline STT model
settings-field-stt_offline_model.notes: Whisper model for offline speech-to-text. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-stt_offline_language.label: Offline STT language
settings-field-stt_offline_language.notes: Language hint for offline transcription. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-image_model.label: Image generation model
settings-field-image_model.notes: Model used for image generation. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-video_gen_model.label: Video generation model
settings-field-video_gen_model.notes: Model used for video generation. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-tts_model.label: Speech model
settings-field-tts_model.notes: Model used for text-to-speech. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-web_search_strategy.label: Web search strategy
settings-field-web_search_strategy.notes: Provider used for web search. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-web_search_brave_api_key.label: Brave API key
settings-field-web_search_brave_api_key.notes: Stored Brave search key; never echoed. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-web_search_serper_api_key.label: Serper API key
settings-field-web_search_serper_api_key.notes: Stored Serper key; never echoed. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-web_search_tavily_api_key.label: Tavily API key
settings-field-web_search_tavily_api_key.notes: Stored Tavily key; never echoed. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-web_answer_provider.label: Web answer provider
settings-field-web_answer_provider.notes: Provider used for web answers. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-web_answer_api_key.label: Web answer API key
settings-field-web_answer_api_key.notes: Stored key for the web answer provider. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-web_answer_model.label: Web answer model
settings-field-web_answer_model.notes: Model used for web answers. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-sound_notifications.label: Sound notifications
settings-field-sound_notifications.notes: Plays a sound when an agent turn completes. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-pets_auto_start.label: Pet auto start
settings-field-pets_auto_start.notes: Launches the desktop pet automatically on start. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-remote_access_enabled.label: Allow remote access
settings-field-remote_access_enabled.notes: Enables remote pairing; mirrored by the remote panel toggle. (id generated at render time)

settings-field-remote_access_addresses.label: Remote access addresses
settings-field-remote_access_addresses.notes: Addresses remote devices can use to reach this instance. (id generated at render time)

settings-preferred-model.label: Preferred model
settings-preferred-model.action: Default model applied to new conversations.

settings-stt-card.label: Offline STT card
settings-stt-card.notes: Install/status card for offline speech-to-text: status copy, checklist, model select, Install/Stop actions, progress, and per-OS install guides.

settings-tts-card.label: Offline TTS card
settings-tts-card.notes: Install/status card for offline text-to-speech: status copy, voice select, Install action, progress.

settings-pet-action.label: Pet install/launch
settings-pet-action.action: Installs or launches the desktop pet.

settings-font-specimen.label: Font specimen
settings-font-specimen.notes: Shows letters, numbers, symbols, and emoji using the active interface font stack.

settings-font-option.label: Interface font options
settings-font-option.action: Chooses the UI font (stored locally, not synced).

stt-guide.label: STT install guide
stt-guide.action: Per-OS install command panels (linux/windows/macos) shown when the platform is unsupported.

settings-progress.label: Install progress
settings-progress.action: Progress bar, phase, and byte counter for install flows.
settings-progress.notes: Rendered as settings-<kind>-progress inside STT/TTS cards.

settings-remote-group.label: Remote access section
settings-remote-group.notes: Whole section; hidden together with its nav jump link on a paired remote client because pairing management is host-only.

settings-remote-access-enabled.label: Allow remote access
settings-remote-access-enabled.action: Enables or disables non-loopback access; saving the toggle restarts the backend automatically.

pairing-create-btn.label: Generate pairing link
pairing-create-btn.action: Creates a one-time pairing challenge and opens the pairing dialog, which renders the QR, the pairing link, and the manual code.

pairing-panel-status.label: Pairing summary
pairing-panel-status.notes: Persistent state summary of the active challenge (waiting, approved, rejected, expired, paired). It is the live region while the dialog is closed and goes quiet (aria-live=off) while the dialog's own status announces.

pairing-show-qr-btn.label: Show pairing QR
pairing-show-qr-btn.action: Reopens the pairing dialog for the active challenge. Hidden until a challenge exists and once it is no longer pending, so a dead link is never offered again.

pairing-approve-btn.label: Approve pairing
pairing-approve-btn.action: Approves the pending pairing challenge so the remote device can exchange for a session.

pairing-device-label.label: Device label
pairing-device-label.notes: Optional label attached to the approved challenge so the issued session row names the device.

pairing-host-status.label: Pairing status (dialog)
pairing-host-status.notes: Live region announcing the challenge state inside the pairing dialog (waiting, approved, rejected, expired, paired). While the dialog is open it is the only live pairing status region.

pairing-qr-display.label: Pairing QR
pairing-qr-display.notes: QR encoding the pairing URL, rendered client-side. It lives inside the pairing dialog because the dialog's overlay covers the Settings panel; the panel only offers Show pairing QR to bring it back.

pairing-qr-img.label: Pairing QR image
pairing-qr-img.notes: Client-side rendered data-URL QR; its alt text names the encoded pairing URL. Reopening the dialog reuses the identical QR for the same challenge.

pairing-qr-status.label: QR status
pairing-qr-status.notes: Tells the host to scan or copy the link/code, flags a configured address that may be unreachable from the remote device, or reports that QR rendering failed and the manual link/code must be used. Static per challenge, so it is not a second live region next to the challenge status.

pairing-qr-alternatives.label: Additional pairing QR links
pairing-qr-alternatives.notes: Renders one additional QR/link card inside the pairing dialog for each configured address after the first address.

pairing-remote-address.label: Remote address
pairing-remote-address.notes: One absolute HTTP(S) address per line. Persisted in settings and encoded into one QR/link per address; does not change where the core listens.

pairing-address-error.label: Remote address error
pairing-address-error.notes: Inline address feedback: a malformed URL is a blocking error, while a link that cannot be reachable (loopback address, or a non-loopback link while the core listens on loopback only, port/host mismatch vs listen_addr) is a non-blocking warning.

pairing-link-display.label: Pairing link
pairing-link-display.notes: The one-time pairing URL for the first configured address, shown inside the pairing dialog next to Copy link.

pairing-copy-link-btn.label: Copy pairing link
pairing-copy-link-btn.action: Copies the pairing URL to the clipboard.

pairing-code-display.label: Pairing code
pairing-code-display.notes: The one-time manual code for the challenge, shown inside the pairing dialog next to Copy code.

pairing-copy-code-btn.label: Copy pairing code
pairing-copy-code-btn.action: Copies the one-time code to the clipboard.

pairing-sessions-list.label: Paired devices
pairing-sessions-list.notes: Active pairing sessions with per-device revoke; revoked sessions are omitted, while expired sessions stay listed dimmed with an Expired badge until revoked.

pairing-revoke-all-btn.label: Revoke all sessions
pairing-revoke-all-btn.action: Revokes every paired device session and removes them from the list.

pairing-approval-overlay.label: Pairing dialog
pairing-approval-overlay.notes: Body-level host dialog that opens when a challenge is created. It owns the scan surface: QR, pairing link, manual code, the extra-address QR cards, the challenge status, the device label, and the Approve/Reject decision. Closing it leaves the challenge pending and returns the QR to the panel summary's Show pairing QR control.

pairing-approval-message.label: Pairing dialog message
pairing-approval-message.notes: Tells the host to scan the QR with the remote device (or open the link on it) and approve the request.

pairing-approval-close.label: Close pairing dialog
pairing-approval-close.action: Closes the dialog while the host continues polling the pending challenge; the panel summary then offers Show pairing QR.

telemetry-range.label: Report time range
telemetry-range.action: Selects the report period: 1h, 3h, 24h, 7d, 30d, or All.

telemetry-stat-spend.label: Estimated spend
telemetry-stat-spend.notes: Aggregate USD spend for the selected period.

telemetry-stat-requests.label: Requests
telemetry-stat-requests.notes: Total assistant turns with usage data.

telemetry-stat-tokens.label: Tokens recorded
telemetry-stat-tokens.notes: Sum of input + output + cache tokens.

plugins-mobile-back.label: Back to plugins
plugins-mobile-back.action: Returns to the filtered plugin list while keeping the selected plugin.
plugins-mobile-back.notes: Mounted by the plugins controller as the first child of the detail header; visible only at widths through 720px where list and detail show one pane at a time.

learning-atlas-back.label: Back to atlas
learning-atlas-back.action: Returns to the atlas result list while keeping the selected record, query, and kind filter.
learning-atlas-back.notes: Mounted by the learning controller at the top of the atlas layout; visible only at widths through 720px.

learning-experience-back.label: Back to episodes
learning-experience-back.action: Returns to the episode list while keeping the loaded episode and page position.
learning-experience-back.notes: Mounted by the learning controller at the top of the experiences layout; visible only at widths through 720px.

learning-doc-toggle.label: Edit memory document
learning-doc-toggle.action: Expands or collapses the card's memory editor (Edit/Done); the draft text, dirty flag, and character counter survive toggling.
learning-doc-toggle.notes: One per .learning-document-card, mounted by the learning controller; the collapsed state only applies at widths through 720px — desktop keeps both editors expanded.

learning-map-toggle.label: Show map
learning-map-toggle.action: Reveals or hides the overview knowledge-map preview (Show map/Hide map); revealing refits the graph into the now-visible frame.
learning-map-toggle.notes: Mounted by the learning controller on the overview map card; the collapsed state only applies at widths through 720px.

automation-mobile-back.label: Back to history
automation-mobile-back.action: Returns from a run or event detail to the mobile history feed, retaining the filter, selection and scroll position.
automation-mobile-back.notes: Shown only for mobile Runs and Events details through 720px.

learning-sync-state.label: Learning sync status
learning-sync-state.notes: Nonvisual live sync status; no status label takes space beside the tabs.

learning-refresh.label: Refresh Learning
learning-refresh.action: Refreshes Learning data; the icon spins until memory, graph and loaded activity/search requests finish, then stops, including on failure.

providers-device-login.label: Device-code sign in
providers-device-login.action: Shows verification link and code with Copy code and Cancel sign in. Checks approval until completion or expiry; errors restore Sign in for retry.

acp-model-search.label: Search ACP models
acp-model-search.action: Filters advertised ACP model rows without changing the preferred model.
